text: An atium bead, still warm from a Seeker's care.
An atium bead, wrapped in oilcloth and hidden in a drainpipe.
An atium bead, dropped by a Coinshot mid-flight.
An atium bead, sewn into the hem of a beggar's coat.
An atium bead, left as payment for a debt no one will name.
An atium bead, tucked behind a loose brick above a canal lock.
A cook's tally of missed meals, scratched in charcoal on a pantry wall.
A runner's route, memorized then burned, but the ash still holds the shape of the letters.
A note pinned under a loose cobble: 'Two lanterns out means the watch changed early tonight.'
A ledger page torn free, listing names in a hand too careful to be honest.
A child's chalk drawing of a rooftop, with a stick figure jumping between chimneys.
A scrap reading: 'Trust the mists. They keep secrets better than any of us do.'
An atium bead, pressed flat where a merchant's counting scale weighed it and thought better of the sale.
An atium bead, hidden inside a hollowed ledger spine, the pages around it never once opened.
An atium bead, still strung on a snapped cord, dropped somewhere between a counting house and a debtor's door.
An atium bead, wedged under a guild-hall cornerstone, laid there before the mortar dried.
An atium bead, wrapped in a bolt of unsold silk, forgotten in a merchant's back room.
An atium bead, tucked into a gutter grate below a counting-house window, out of reach of careless fingers.
An atium bead, set in a keepsake box a noble house stopped opening generations ago.
An atium bead, resting in the ash of a courtyard brazier that burns every night but this.
An atium bead, dropped by a sentry who never noticed, and never will.
An atium bead, sewn into a footman's livery, a wage he was never paid.
An atium bead, sunk in a mooring-post crack, slick with canal damp.
An atium bead, rolled into a coil of net rope left drying on a jetty.
An atium bead, left as a toll no ferryman ever collected.
An atium bead, half-buried in soot beneath the Lord Ruler's own spires, where no beggar dares dig.
A merchant's private tally, two sets of numbers in the same careful hand: one for the Canton, one for himself.
A torn invoice for 'sundries', the amount scratched out three times and never settled.
A guild apprentice's note: 'Master says the numbers balance. Master is lying to somebody. I don't think it's us.'
A pressed flower between two receipts, the ink long since bled into the petals.
A steward's memorandum: 'The young lord asks too many questions for a man his father trusts so little.'
A dance-card corner, one name circled twice and crossed out once.
A page from a house genealogy, one branch of the family tree inked over so thick the names beneath are lost.
A folded reminder in a servant's hand: 'Do not let the master see the guest list until after the ball.'
A dock ledger page, cargo weights that don't match the cargo, in ink still faintly damp.
A bargeman's note pinned to a post: 'Toll's gone up again. Ask me how much of it reaches the canton.'
A child's boat carved from driftwood, one oar missing, left where the current couldn't take it.
A stevedore's tally stick, notches worn smooth by a thumb that counted them every night before sleep.
A prayer scratched into a paving stone at the foot of the spires, in a hand too unsteady to have finished it.
A single glove, fine leather, dropped by someone who never once looked back for it.
